Theme

School & learning

lecture noun

also lectures, give a lecture, go to a lecture

classical

Cic. Tusc. 1.7–8: scholās Graecōrum mōre habēre
Suet. Tib. 11.3
M-O s.v. class, after Egger

schola, scholae f.

noun, first declension

a lecture, a learned talk

Greek σχολή, leisure and what scholars do with it: a lecture or a learned discussion, and then the place where it is given, a school (Lewis & Short). To give a lecture is scholam habēre; to attend a teacher’s lectures, simply audīre (tē, Marce fīlī, annum jam audientem Cratippum, Cic. Off. 1.1).

Other words

  • 1acroāsis: short first a (Lewis & Short ācroāsis, without evidence). Greek ἀκρόασις, from ἀκροάομαι, with the short ἀ of ἄκρος; Lewis & Short marks the same a short in acrochordon, acropodium, acrōtēria, also from ἄκρος.

    acroāsis1, acroāsis f. — a public lecture

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 15.17.2: vel in acroāsī audeam legere; Suet. Gram. 2 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 339; M-O s.v. lecture

    Greek ἀκρόασις, a hearing: a lecture or reading before an audience. To give one, acroāsin facere (Suet. Gram. 2; Traupman 339).

  • praelēctiō, praelēctiōnis f. — a reading of a text aloud, with explanation

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Quint. 1.2.15; 2.5.4 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 339

    The teacher reads a text aloud and explains it (see read aloud, praelegere); Lewis & Short: post-Augustan.

Examples

  • ut jam etiam scholās Graecōrum mōre habēre audērēmus … itaque diērum quīnque scholās, ut Graecī appellant, in totidem librōs contulī

    so that I even dared to give lectures in the Greek manner … so I have gathered the five days’ lectures, as the Greeks call them, into as many booksCic. Tusc. 1.7–8

  • ipsīus litterae sīc et φιλοστόργως et εὐπινῶς scrīptae ut eās vel in acroāsī audeam legere

    his own letters are written so affectionately and so elegantly that I would dare to read them out even at a public lectureCic. Att. 15.17.2

  • acroāsin facere

    to give a lectureTraupman 339

  • sermōnem habēre

    to give a talkTraupman 339

See also professor, university, lesson, student, read aloud.
